newsitem.title: USA: Snow, flooding delay Minnesota spring plantings.
newsitem.headline: Snow, flooding delay Minnesota spring plantings.

text.p: Snow, flooding and wintry cold have delayed the start of spring planting preparations in in many parts of Minnesota, according to the state's Agricultural Statistic Service.

"Much of the cropland which lies within the valleys of the Red River and its tributaries has been inundated by floodwater as the record snowpack over northwestern Minnesota melts slowly," the weekly crop report said.
For the week ended April 20, none of the spring wheat crop was planted, versus two percent last year and the five-year average of nine percent.

None of the barley crop was planted, the same as last year but behind the five-year average of five percent. Three percent of the oat crop was planted, compared to the five-year average of 11 percent, the report said.
Two percent of the corn fields had been prepared for planting, compared to one percent last week and the five-year average of seven percent.

The average date for full-scale fieldwork is April 29. The northwest part of the state, which produces most of the state's spring wheat and barley, will see a much later average startup date, the report said.

"The actual commencement of full-scale field activities will depend upon weather conditions," according to the report. "Additional moisture could prolong flooding in river valleys and delay entry into fields elsewhere."
Topsoil moisture was rated 45 percent adequate and 52 percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was rated 47 percent adequate and 51 percent surplus.
